points.why: It says the reviewer only sees article text and guidelines, so it can't detect UI drift, and a stricter prompt runs the same kind of check harder.
It proposes replaying the steps in a staging build with a script or UI test, and tying articles to product areas so releases trigger re-verification.
It notes that auto-publishing leaves no human whose job is to notice, and gates deletion, billing and export articles behind human sign-off, but it never recommends mapping who reviews what.
It says 98% approval is not evidence the review works and reframes the outcome as 'nothing the current checks can see is wrong,' not 'the articles are right.'

pitfalls.why: It explicitly says a stricter prompt cannot address this incident and is at most a cheap add-on.
